author: Russell Brand
description:
JD Vance laid out the uncomfortable reality that American taxpayers fund an entire European ally's defense while that same ally jails its own citizens over online speech. He argued real friendship between nations requires shared values, and those values don't exist if elections get cancelled or people get silenced for wanting secure borders. Russell called it an extraordinary piece of analysis, agreeing the relationship deserves far more scrutiny than it gets. Some takes land because they're simply too honest to ignore.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Nancy Pelosi tore up a plastic crown to symbolize her stance against corrupt power, and Russell couldn't let the gesture pass without a response. He suggested she turn that same energy inward, questioning why she'd need to stop profiting from information gained in Congress if corruption really was the enemy. Russell argued invoking children only when convenient isn't the same as actually doing something for them. Sometimes the loudest symbols of resistance are standing closest to the thing they claim to fight.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell opened up about the first sober event he ever went to, admitting he still had burned foils in his jacket pocket and no real intention of staying clean. He recalled telling a friend he'd be dead at 27, convinced he wasn't built for a life without drugs, only to realize years later he'd only had six months left of actually being 27 when he said it. Russell reflected on how far removed he now feels from that person, and how far he'll likely feel from who he is today. Growth doesn't announce itself, it just quietly happens one day at a time.

author: Russell Brand
description: Russell watched a red carpet clip of Elon Musk moving and decided it looked exactly like a character straight out of The Sims. He joked that Musk learned his behavior so deeply from gaming, being reportedly one of the best players in the world, that he ended up mimicking it in real life. Russell compared it to his own relationship with television, admitting some people just get embedded in a reality until it becomes their own. Sometimes the funniest observations are the ones that are a little too accurate.
title: Elon Musk Moves Like A Video Game Character!

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell questioned the panic over banning TikTok, asking why nobody applies the same scrutiny to Facebook and Google's relationship with the American government. He argued every platform manipulates its algorithm, so the real issue isn't which country is doing it, it's whether the institutions claiming to protect you actually see you as an enemy. Russell pointed to the language of extremism and hate being used against ordinary people as proof the threat isn't coming from where they say it is. If control of your feed is the concern, maybe look closer to home first.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell broke down the irony of Billie Eilish speaking out against stolen land while her own mansion sits on ground once occupied by the Tongva tribe, with no record of her contacting them directly. He argued she'd proven the real problem with wokeness, an ideology that preaches justice loudly but doesn't notice when its own believers are doing the exact thing it condemns. Reflecting on his own years at the Grammys and MTV Awards, Russell admitted something always felt off about the whole performance. Sometimes the loudest values are the ones nobody applies to themselves first.
